classification.classification_note: The saved crash is an AddressSanitizer stack-use-after-scope READ. Source-wise, `OverlayNG::computeEdgeOverlay()` stores the address of block-local stack `clipEnv` in `EdgeNodingBuilder`, the block ends, and later clipping logic dereferences that expired stack object through `clipEnv->disjoint(env)`.

bug_description.original: A security vulnerability exists where the stack allocated envelope is not properly ensured to be available to edgeNodingBuilder, potentially leading to unsafe behavior.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 60-byte `fuzz_geo2` witness is split at its first NUL byte: bytes `[0, 19)` are WKT `LINESTRING(7 0,7 0)` and bytes `[19, 60)` are the second geometry's WKB blob beginning with big-endian byte-order `0x00`. In `GEOSGeomFromWKT_r`, the prefix is first copied into `wktstring` and then parsed into `g1`; the suffix WKB parse yields `g2`, so the harness reaches `GEOSIntersection(g1, g2)`. On that path `OverlayNG::getResult()` selects `computeEdgeOverlay()`, which enters the optimized clipping block, declares stack `Envelope clipEnv`, fills it via `OverlayUtil::clippingEnvelope()`, and passes `&clipEnv` into `EdgeNodingBuilder::setClipEnvelope()`. Vulnerable code stores that pointer in the builder even though `clipEnv` is scoped only inside the `if (isOptimized)` block. After the block ends, `nodingBuilder.build()` immediately reuses the dangling pointer from `EdgeNodingBuilder::add()` through `isClippedCompletely()` and `clipEnv->disjoint(env)`. AddressSanitizer reports a stack-use-after-scope READ at `include/geos/geom/Envelope.inl:283`, and its frame report identifies the accessed stack object as `clipEnv` from `OverlayNG.cpp:218`. The patch fixes the bug by moving `Envelope clipEnv;` outside the `if` so the same pointer remains valid for the whole lifetime of `nodingBuilder`.

source.description: First project-side consumption of attacker input on the crashing path. `GEOSGeomFromWKT_r` copies the incoming buffer into owned `std::string` state, creating the exact WKT text that the later reader turns into `g1`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 60 bytes (sha256 `b59f7c4d74e7f20ac486181db25512ed4fda72998f6197f467dafecadc4edf9d`). `fuzz_geo2` stops at the first NUL at offset 19 and passes that same buffer to `GEOSGeomFromWKT`; this statement therefore materializes bytes `[0, 19)` as the string `LINESTRING(7 0,7 0)`.

sink.description: ASan sink. Here `this` is the expired stack `clipEnv`, so evaluating the disjointness predicate reads dead stack fields from that out-of-scope `Envelope` object.

root_cause.description: Root cause. Vulnerable code hands `EdgeNodingBuilder` the address of block-local stack `clipEnv`, even though that object dies at the end of the enclosing `if (isOptimized)` block before later builder operations reuse it.
root_cause.note: The patch keeps the same call but moves `Envelope clipEnv;` out of the inner block, extending the pointed object's lifetime until after `nodingBuilder.build()` returns.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first concrete attacker-shaped project state is the owned `wktstring` copy built from bytes before the first NUL. Step 2 parses this string into geometry `g1`, whose envelope later becomes the `env` argument at the stale-pointer dereference.

parser_admitted.description: Both geometry parses succeeded, so the harness entered the first overlay operation and called `GEOSIntersection(g1, g2)`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness splits the input at the first NUL, parses the prefix as WKT and the suffix starting at that NUL as WKB, then calls `GEOSIntersection(g1, g2)`.
Optimized edge overlay allocates stack `clipEnv`, computes the clipping envelope into it, and passes `&clipEnv` into `EdgeNodingBuilder`.
After the optimized block has ended, builder state still holds the escaped pointer and `add()` reuses it from `isClippedCompletely()`.
The stale clip-envelope pointer is dereferenced as an `Envelope` object and ASan reports a stack-use-after-scope READ from expired stack storage.

fine_trace.note: Source. The buffer passed from the harness is first consumed here as a C string; because the first NUL is at offset 19, this statement materializes bytes `[0, 19)` as `wktstring == "LINESTRING(7 0,7 0)"`.
`WKTReader` parses the attacker-controlled string from step 1 and yields the first non-null geometry `g1`, a line geometry later passed into the overlay path that crashes.

Because step 2 succeeded, the harness also parses bytes `[19, 60)` beginning at the separator NUL as WKB. `WKBReader` accepts that exact big-endian payload, masks the type word down to geometry type `2`, reads point count `2`, and materializes the second non-null geometry `g2`.

The first harnessed operation is `GEOSIntersection(g1, g2)`. Since both parsed inputs are edge geometries rather than point-only inputs, overlay dispatch reaches the vulnerable edge-overlay implementation.

fine_trace.code:
Envelope clipEnv;
bool gotClipEnv = OverlayUtil::clippingEnvelope(opCode, &inputGeom, pm, clipEnv);
fine_trace.note: Inside the taken optimized block, vulnerable code allocates stack `clipEnv` and fills it from the two input-geometry envelopes. On the witnessed intersection path this helper returns `gotClipEnv == true`, so the stack object now holds the clipping extent that builder code will later consult.

Root cause. The builder receives the address of the block-local stack object from step 5, even though that object's lifetime is limited to the current `if (isOptimized)` block. The patch fixes this exact escape by moving the declaration out of the inner scope.

The builder stores that escaped stack address in member `clipEnv`, which is the member later reused by `isClippedCompletely()`. This call also initializes clipping helpers, but the witnessed stale dereference depends on the builder member rather than on a helper-held alias.

After control has left the optimized block in `computeEdgeOverlay()`, `clipEnv` is already out of scope, but `nodingBuilder.build()` immediately starts processing the first parsed geometry while the builder member still points at that expired stack object.

The first `add()` call is on `geom0` from step 2. Because `g1` is non-null and not empty, this guard asks whether its envelope is completely clipped, reusing builder member `clipEnv` after the original stack object has expired.

fine_trace.code:
if (clipEnv == nullptr) return false;
return clipEnv->disjoint(env);
fine_trace.note: The stale builder member is non-null, so clipping logic falls through to a method call on the expired `Envelope` object instead of skipping clipping. The valid geometry envelope from step 9 becomes the `env` argument.

fine_trace.code:
return !(other->minx <= maxx ||
             other->maxx >= minx ||
             other->miny <= maxy ||
             other->maxy >= miny);
fine_trace.note: Sink. Step 10 dispatches through dangling `clipEnv`, so this predicate reads the dead fields of that expired stack object. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `stack-use-after-scope` with `READ of size 8` here and identifies `clipEnv` from `OverlayNG::computeEdgeOverlay()` line 218 as the poisoned stack slot.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: ASan's frame report points to stack object `clipEnv` at `OverlayNG::computeEdgeOverlay()` line 218, and the fine trace shows that step 6 escapes `&clipEnv` out of that inner block before later reuse.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The patch moves `Envelope clipEnv;` from inside the `if (isOptimized)` block to function scope, so the pointer passed at step 6 stays valid until after `nodingBuilder.build()` returns.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The saved `sanitizer_trace.txt` reports `stack-use-after-scope` at `Envelope.inl:283` and explicitly names `clipEnv` at `OverlayNG.cpp:218` as the poisoned stack object; the patch diff makes the same lifetime repair in the staged vulnerable source.

format.name: fuzz_geo2 WKT+WKB pair
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 60-byte witness `poc` (sha256 `b59f7c4d74e7f20ac486181db25512ed4fda72998f6197f467dafecadc4edf9d`) as interpreted by `fuzz_geo2`. The harness scans to the first NUL byte at offset 19, passes bytes `[0, 19)` to `GEOSGeomFromWKT`, and passes bytes `[19, 60)` starting at that same NUL to `GEOSGeomFromWKB_buf`. For this witness, the WKT prefix must remain `LINESTRING(7 0,7 0)` so the first parse yields non-null line geometry `g1`, and the suffix must remain an accepted big-endian WKB LineString with point count `2` whose coordinate doubles are all `0x2020202020202020`, so the second parse yields non-null line geometry `g2`. Both parses must succeed so the first operation `GEOSIntersection(g1, g2)` reaches optimized `OverlayNG::computeEdgeOverlay()`, stores `&clipEnv` in `EdgeNodingBuilder`, and later calls `add()` after `clipEnv` has gone out of scope. This contract is limited to that exact harness split and witnessed intersection path; it does not generalize to other separators, encodings, or geometry pairs.
